title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-18
content:
Morning checklist / context:
- Quick notes while triaging cluster capacity and network flakiness.
- Goal: keep Dedicated pools within SLA, avoid noisy-neighbor spikes, ensure KV cache warmups for 8k sequences.

TODAY (2026-03-04) top priorities:
1) GPU pool balancing (high priority)
   - Observed 20% higher tail latency on pool-gpu-v3 at 02:00 PST. Suspect uneven autoscaler bin-packing after canary rollout.
   - Action: run binpack-sim and manually drain slot on node g3-12-07 to rebalance.
   - Commands to run later: 
     - ./infra/bin/binpack-sim --pool pool-gpu-v3 --dry-run
     - gcloud compute instances reset g3-12-07 --zone=us-west1-b (confirm with SRE)
   - Notes: schedule small canary post-rebalance for customer-facing endpoints only.

2) Networking jitter on private deployments (medium)
   - Multiple customer logs show re-synced TCP sessions during SG updates. Looked at firewall rules audit; last change 2026-03-02 by infra-automation.
   - Task: correlate firewall audit id with customer incidents; open follow-up with NetEng.
   - Quick mitigation: enable connection-draining for control-plane LB for next maintenance window.

3) KV cache warmups for long-context workloads (low/ongoing)
   - Idea: prewarm KV cache using synthetic prefix requests for tail-heavy customers. Prototype script exists under runtime/tools/kv-prewarm.
   - TODO: test at 10% traffic, measure token-cost delta and p50 latency improvement.

Quick wins / TODOs:
- [ ] Add autoscaler threshold metrics to pool dashboards (p99 latency, cpu_util, free_slots) - ticket JIRA-OPS-490
- [x] Rebooted g2-08-03 last night (confirmed improved GC cycles)
- [ ] Draft runbook snippet for network-driven session resets and mitigation steps
- [ ] Sync w/ Maya on Dedicated capacity forecasting for Q2

Notes from overnight alerts:
- Alert: pool-gpu-v3-high-tail-latency (3 triggers between 02:00-03:15)
  - Runner logs show GPU utilization spike + increased context-switches on host kernel (maybe driver issue).
  - Kernel messages: "NVRM: Xid 31" on one host - escalate to HW team? Add to hardware watchlist.

Random/ideas:
- Consider adding mini-janitor job that proactively evicts stale KV entries older than 48h for v2 models to reduce memory tails.
- Evaluate q8_0 quantization on 8k context models; check perf delta in staging.

Meeting notes (standup 09:30):
- Maya: will investigate autoscaler logs and provide diff by EOD.
- Jordan: working on LB draining config; aiming for test on staging tomorrow.
- Me: manual rebalance + post-rollout canary for pool-gpu-v3.

Stuff to follow up on:
- Get GH PR review for runtime/pool-binning (#712) merged before manual drain. If blocked, coordinate with Release Eng for emergency patch window.
- Confirm with Security that prewarm synthetic traffic is ok for customer-managed private deployments.

Notes-to-self:
- When doing manual drain, annotate the node with reason "tail-latency-rebalance-2026-03-04" and add link to this scratchpad.
- Keep an eye on per-route token cost spikes when enabling prewarm.

End-of-day quick summary (to paste into ticket):
- Completed: reboot g2-08-03, ran preliminary binpack-sim (dry run).
- Next: schedule node drain on g3-12-07 pending PR merge, follow up with NetEng on firewall audit correlation.

References/links (local):
- infra runbooks: confluence://infra/runbooks/gpu-pool-drain
- KV prewarm prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/kv-prewarm
- Autoscaler metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/auto/pool-autoscaler

End.
